chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabie who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the miscarried child (saqit), when it falls from the belly of its mother, if it moves with a distinct movement, it inherits and is inherited from, for perhaps it was mute.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a miscarried fetus to inherit and be inherited from in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the criterion of 'distinct movement' (haraka bayyin) for a fetus to acquire legal personality (shakhsiyya qanuniyya) in Shia jurisprudence, allowing it to inherit and be inherited. It clarifies that sensory defects like muteness do not negate this status, emphasizing that physical viability and movement are the key indicators for inheritance rights before full birth. This ruling is foundational in fiqh for determining the share of the unborn child in estate distribution.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the miscarried child, when it is miscarried from the belly of its mother, so it moves. Manifest movement makes him inherit and be inherited from, for perhaps it was mute’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib‘iy who has narrated the following: “

I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘If a miscarried child falls off the womb of his mother and moves with clear movement, he inherits and is inherited; perhaps he is speechless so that he did not cry.’”
